Controller/route wiring for creating or approving a real `tool-install` proposal end-to-end (no generator exists yet for this kind, matching D1.1's precedent that model/validator phases land ahead of any generator).
judgment_calls: The pre-existing untracked test skeleton did not include `testPrompts` in its shared `validChangeJson` fixture even though the acceptance criteria require rejecting missing/unbounded/mistyped test prompts. Added `testPrompts` to the fixture and 8 new test cases (missing, empty, mistyped entry, over-count, over-length/raw-blob-with-no-echo, in-bounds accept, closed-set installMethod rejection, local-script rejection) rather than leaving that criterion uncovered.

Check ORDER inside `validateToolInstallChange` was chosen deliberately so the pre-existing 'missing evidence bundle entirely' test (whose fixture also omits testPrompts) still reports 'evidenceBundle' rather than 'testPrompts': required-4-fields → installMethod closed-set → evidenceBundle presence/shape → testPrompts shape/bounds → agentConfigId existence → target ref/hash fabrication check.

`testPrompts` bounds (max 20 entries, max 4000 chars/entry) are new, undocumented-elsewhere constants chosen as schema hygiene against unbounded `change_json` blobs — not derived from any existing limit in the codebase, since none exists for this shape yet.

Production install-method registry (`npm install`, `pip install`) intentionally excludes `tool_sandbox_vetter.ts`'s `local-script` TEST-ONLY escape hatch, per that module's own doc comment forward-referencing 'the production proposal validator in D1.3'.

The pre-existing test skeleton's `beforeEach` called a nonexistent `configsRepo.create(...)` method (typo/stale API) — fixed to the real `AgentConfigsRepository.insert({label, icon, systemPrompt})` API, and its first assertion (`result.reason` on a VALID result) called `.not.toMatch()` on `undefined`, which vitest throws on — fixed with `result.reason ?? ''`. Neither fix touches this issue's actual validation logic.

No raw-prompt-persistence check beyond the validator's own reason strings: this module performs no database write and no console/logger call of any kind, so there is no additional persistence/logging surface to test directly — the invariant is upheld by the module simply never touching `testPrompts` content outside the bounds check.
